value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse data dictionary
variable_description: What kind of organisation runs the aged care service: for-profit, not-for-profit or government. Ownership purpose is one of the few provider attributes that is stable over a service's life and it cuts across almost every aged care outcome, so it is the usual first cut when comparing services. It describes the approved provider, not the individual site, so a provider running many services carries one value across all of them.
value_definition: A small set of ownership categories. The AIHW reports aged care activity against these three groupings, and government here means a state, territory or local government provider rather than Commonwealth funding, which nearly every provider receives.
limitation: Ownership purpose is not a measure of quality, size or fee structure, and the not-for-profit group mixes religious, charitable and community providers that differ from one another as much as they differ from for-profit providers. A provider that changes hands takes the new owner's purpose from that point, so a service's history can switch category without anything about the care changing.
rationale: The AIHW data dictionary defines the provider attributes carried in the National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse, and the AIHW reports aged care activity split by provider ownership.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, so the page still said 'not specified' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse data dictionary
variable_description: The kind of dwelling the care recipient usually lives in, recorded at assessment. It is the column that separates someone living in a private home from someone already in supported or residential accommodation, which is the difference between a home-support pathway and a residential one. Because it is captured at assessment it describes where the person was living when assessed, not where they went afterwards.
value_definition: A category naming the dwelling type. Private dwellings, retirement villages, supported residential services and residential aged care are the distinctions the assessment turns on.
limitation: The value is a snapshot at assessment and does not update when the person moves, so it cannot be used to track a transition into residential care; the care-type and service records do that. It describes the dwelling rather than the household, so it says nothing about whether the person lives alone, which the carer columns carry instead.
rationale: The AIHW data dictionary defines the accommodation attributes recorded against an aged care assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, so the page still said 'not specified' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: Whether the care recipient has someone providing them unpaid care. It is the single strongest predictor in the file of how long someone can stay at home, because an informal carer substitutes for a large share of formal service hours, and it is also what makes a recipient's own service use hard to read on its own. A recipient with no carer using few services is a different situation from one with a carer using few services.
value_definition: An indicator of whether a carer exists, not a count and not a measure of how much care they give. The related carer columns describe the relationship and the living arrangement.
limitation: The indicator records whether a carer was identified at assessment, so it undercounts: carers who do not name themselves as such, and care that begins after assessment, are both invisible. It says nothing about the carer's own capacity or health, which is what actually determines whether the arrangement holds.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the carer attributes recorded against a care recipient in the Data Exchange, which is the collection this clearinghouse field is drawn from.
